pos.personaBrief: El Gráfico 1975 shows Independiente ceding the ball (rival had more possession) and controlling the game through defensive organisation and counter-attacks, so possession was not the goal.

pro.personaBrief: Counter-attacks after regaining the ball and Bertoni-Bochini one-twos; safe, adult game with few risks from the back.

est.personaBrief: Clockwork defensive mechanism with defined roles, but attack built on Bochini-Bertoni wall-passes and a roaming no. 8 who covers.

lar.personaBrief: Wingers could not win a desborde per El Gráfico; goals came from central wall-passes among Bochini, Bertoni and Raimondo.

blo.personaBrief: Achique and offside line, but the 1973 match was played mostly in their own half and the team waited and countered rather than pressing high.

mar.personaBrief: Achique with offside trap suggests collective line, yet El Gráfico cites hombres de marca; era-typical Argentine individual marking at corners and on stars.

pla.personaBrief: Same calculated, patient counter-attacking identity under rotating coaches, leading the rival to the business that suited Independiente; plan kept.

res.personaBrief: Four Libertadores and Intercontinental won with cold administration of matches and defensive organisation that was enough to win; results first.

sis.personaBrief: Everyone worked (Bochini and Ruiz Moreno dropped back, the 8 marked) within a well-calculated system, though Bochini had creative licence.

jog.personaBrief: Mix of brains and brawn per These Football Times: technical Bochini and Bertoni alongside rough-house tactics and marking midfielders.

bas.personaBrief: Young Bochini and Bertoni in attack but experienced defenders (Sa, Pavoni, Commisso); El Gráfico says the kids need the veterans' work in finals.

lid.personaBrief: Revolving door of managers, with players taking on game control themselves; little evidence of a harmonious management style, discipline and professional order implied.
